newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran completes four days of wargames in the Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Iran completes four days of wargames in the Gulf.

text.p: Iran completed four days of amphibious wargames in the Gulf designed to heighten the military's ability to protect its coastal borders, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said on Thursday.
The exercises, which included the bombing of mock enemy targets, were conducted by units of Iran's army and the naval forces of its Revolutionary Guards, IRNA said.
Ground, naval and air units of Iran's Revolutionary Guards in late April staged the country's largest Gulf wargames, codenamed "Tariq ol-Qods" (Road to Jerusalem).
The exercises, which involved 200,000 members of the guards and Basij militia volunteers, covered four provinces stretching from the mouth of the Gulf to the border with Iraq.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards commander was quoted earlier this week as saying Iran had no intention of starting a war, but said it would turn the region into a slaughterhouse for U.S. forces if they attacked.

"Iran will never start any war, but if the Americans one day decide to attack us, then they would have committed suicide. We will turn the region into a slaughterhouse for them. There is no place better than the Persian Gulf to destroy America's might," Major General Mohsen Rezaie said.
